approved_findings: The new and matched old captures have the same withdrawal lifecycle: cardholder asks the issuer to cancel a financial chargeback, but withdrawal does not itself mean a win, speed resolution, change Dashboard/API display, or remove the network dispute-rate count (new raw:13-23; old raw:12-22). EFWs and inquiries cannot be fully withdrawn.

Both captures require timely, one-shot evidence submission for a merchant seeking a favorable outcome even after a customer says they withdrew, and both say a refund on a disputed charge stays blocked until the issuer decides for the merchant (new raw:35-47; old raw:34-46). Customer withdrawal confirmation is helpful, explicitly not required.

Both captures preserve fee and decision boundaries: a countered fee may apply in addition to the received fee; it is returned on a win, while the received fee generally is not; Mexico and Japan are excepted from the countered fee (new raw:49-53; old raw:48-52). The cardholder's bank, not Stripe or customer agreement, decides the dispute, potentially over up to three months.

Both captures say card networks permit late withdrawal even after a loss, but some issuers may not support it in every case (new raw:61; old raw:60). Late adjustments often occur outside the regular network lifecycle: the issuer might take weeks or months to process one, while a realistic date for its reflection in Stripe is difficult to set (new raw:63; old raw:62). Correct current source:38,40 and disputes concept:133; the existing summaries overstate issuer acceptance and the timing certainty. This is a pre-existing retained-claim correction, not a new November rule.

Diff 1-74 changes italic markup, heading whitespace, blockquote padding, and adds three see-also links. These are presentational/navigation changes, with no new withdrawal rule, eligibility condition, timing promise, fee condition, or refund transition.
approved_conflicts: Current source wiki/sources/source-stripe-disputes-withdrawals.md:38 and concept wiki/concepts/disputes.md:133 say all networks allow post-deadline withdrawal but omit the adjacent issuer-specific limitation (old raw:60; new raw:61). Correct both: network permission does not guarantee the particular card issuer accepts a late withdrawal; the cardholder must contact that issuer to determine whether it is allowed.
